acceptanceCriteria: A valid repository-bound custom evidence projection no longer blocks verification preconditions.
Missing, stale, malformed, foreign, symlinked, and non-regular custom evidence still fail closed before project process spawn.
Regression tests prove project process spawn is zero on invalid projections and preserve structured precondition attempt evidence.
The same Work Item rule is documented for future Agent execution and does not create a successor for a same-root problem.
Exact full Work Item IDs in parity rows are recognized deterministically, while legacy short IDs remain supported and unrelated rows remain fail-closed.
MCP verification uses the same repository-bound precondition and zero-spawn attempt persistence as the CLI entry point.
A repository-bound verification that cannot complete its lifecycle projection leaves no partial completion evidence and preserves the execution attempt for later recovery.
MCP rejects invalid Work Item identifiers before repository-bound verification can spawn a project process.
A successful execution whose formal receipt cannot be recorded is classified as execution_completed with a diagnostic that preserves the recording failure cause.

A failed project command or timeout is persisted as a non-reusable execution failure, never as execution_completed or completion evidence, with its exit code, timeout, elapsed time, bounded logs, and input identity preserved.

A reusable verification attempt is accepted only when its content digest, embedded receipt identity, repository identity, Work Item identity, Runtime identity, command identity, and successful execution records all match the current request; any tampering or mismatch invalidates reuse while preserving the bytes for diagnosis.
Verification projection rollback reports any restoration failure instead of silently claiming rollback, and normal failures leave the pre-existing projection bytes unchanged.
goal: Allow valid custom evidence projections to pass the precondition gate before project verification, with regression coverage for valid, stale, malformed, and missing projections.
intent: Fix the verification precondition boundary so correctly repository-bound custom evidence classes do not block project verification, while malformed or stale evidence remains fail-closed.

scenarioCoverage.expected: A complete custom evidence projection bound to the current repository, Contract digest, and Runtime identity does not block verification before the project command starts.
scenarioCoverage.scenario: valid repository-bound custom evidence permits verification preconditions
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Run the focused preflight regression with a regular current-digest evidence file and assert that the project command starts and the persisted precondition attempt is successful.

scenarioCoverage.expected: Missing, stale, malformed, foreign, symlinked, and non-regular custom evidence each fail closed with zero project processes spawned and a persisted structured attempt.
scenarioCoverage.scenario: invalid custom evidence is rejected before project process spawn
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Run focused precondition tests for each invalid projection and inspect the attempt fields, exit status, and diagnostic identity.

scenarioCoverage.expected: Node exit code, timeout state, duration, logs, and input identity remain available even when governance rejects the formal completion receipt.
scenarioCoverage.scenario: failed execution result remains durable when formal receipt cannot be written
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Run the focused executor persistence regression with an intentionally rejected formal receipt and inspect the independent attempt evidence.

scenarioCoverage.expected: A governance-only Contract correction can reuse unchanged execution inputs, while code, command, dependency, or relevant configuration changes invalidate reuse.
scenarioCoverage.scenario: only governance-bound changes permit safe result reuse
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Run the focused reuse identity regression across unchanged, governance-only, and execution-input-changed cases.
